newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN DERBY SET TO BREAK BOX-OFFICE RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN DERBY SET TO BREAK BOX-OFFICE RECORD.

text.p: Italian champions AC Milan meet serie A leaders Internazionale in the 65th Milan league derby on Sunday in a match which seems certain to set a box-office record.

By Thursday evening 78,355 tickets had been sold, making it probable that Sunday night's takings will surpass the $2.2 million dollars paid out by 82,788 spectators to watch Milan v Juventus in October 1995.
Adding extra spice to an always keenly anticipated derby is the fact that Inter are having their best season for years.

Out in front in the league and recent 3-0 winners against Juventus in an Italian Cup tie, Inter confirmed their current good form with an easy 5-1 win against Portuguese side Boavista in a midweek UEFA Cup tie.
AC Milan, after an unusually shaky start to the season which saw them lose six games in the first two months, appear to be finding their best form.
Milan were far from disgraced in a 1-1 Champions' League draw away to Portuguese champions Porto on Wednesday.
Only the dreadful state of the San Siro pitch threatens to spoil the evening's entertainment.
Grass has not grown properly at the San Siro for six seasons now, forcing the two clubs to resort to the short-term solution of regular returfing.
During heavy rain, such as has fallen in northern Italy over the last fortnight, the San Siro becomes an unplayable quagmire.
Partial returfing has been going on all week but has been hampered by the difficulties of importing turf sods from Bordeaux because of a truck drivers' strike in France.
Recent records suggest that there will be little to choose between the two sides with the last six league derbies seeing two wins apiece and two draws.
Both sides are expected to be at full strength with Roberto Baggio and Liberian George Weah leading the Milan attack and with Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff and Chilean Ivan Zamorano up front for Inter.

Milan captain Franco Baresi again leads his side from central defence, allowing Frenchman Marcel Desailly to return to midfield alongside Demetrio Albertini, Croat Zvonimir Boban and Dutchman Edgar Davids.
Englishman Paul Ince returns to the Inter midfield alongside Argentine Javier Zanetti, Dutchman Aron Winter and Salvatore Fresi.

Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson, who this week extended his contract with the club through to June 1999, expects a good match, saying: "As far as I'm concerned, there already is a winner of this game and it is the paying public who on Sunday night...can say they have seen a spectacle."
